endorsements.quote: Therefore, it is essential to familiarize patients with the benefits and limitations of AI in health care to gain their trust and support.
Digital competencies could also be taught to graduated HCP through continued education forums on digital health care, scientific meetings, conferences, and datathon and hackathon events.

unlisted_practices: Incorporate digital health and AI competencies into health care professional training curricula, including classes, web-based courses, and certifications.
Teach trainees fundamental AI concepts, including taxonomy, data sets, workflow integration, bias, and human-machine interaction.
Establish a Clinical AI medical specialty to lead safer AI deployment and regulation and to continuously review and recalibrate AI models.
Integrate new digital competencies into existing program components to overcome curriculum time constraints.
Teach health care professionals to critically appraise AI studies, including data set quality, external validation, and operating threshold adequacy.
Form partnerships among developers, professional societies, academia, and specialists from different backgrounds, including social scientists, to advance digital health literacy.
Have social scientists analyze the sociocultural implications of health technologies to avoid biases and dangerous AI results.
Developers should give explicit assurances of commitment to data privacy to build patient trust.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article discussing digital education, competencies, and workforce training needed for the safe deployment and governance of AI in healthcare.
